name: Lingomize Translator
author: gvnmarketing

sections.description:
Lingomize rewrites the page HTML on its way out, so every language is the same post
with different words. Nothing is duplicated, so nothing drifts.

  • Automatic /th/, /fr/, … URLs with correct hreflang
  • Point-and-click editing on the live page
  • A translation table for the whole site, with search and bulk editing
  • Glossary and a keep-as-is term list
  • Import / export as JSON, and a one-click import from WPML, Polylang, TranslatePress or Weglot
  • Language switcher with flags
  • AI translation, with a licence key

Licence

AI translation runs through the Lingomize licence proxy, which holds the AI key. Paste the
key from your welcome email under Lingomize → Settings. While the subscription is live the
site serves every language; let it lapse and the site goes back to its own language until
it is renewed. Your translations are never deleted — they stay in your database and come
back the moment the licence does. A site holding more original words than its plan covers
keeps every translation it has, but gets no new ones until it is upgraded or trimmed.

External services

The plugin contacts one address, only once a licence key is set. That service uses one model
provider behind it; both are described below. Nothing else leaves your server — the switcher’s flags ship with
the plugin, and no image, script or stylesheet is loaded from anywhere but your own site.

Lingomize licence proxy (https://api.lingomize.com)
Every translation request and the daily licence check go through it. Sent: the text you
chose to translate, the target language, the optional style notes you typed under Settings
(what the site is about, tone, audience), your licence key, your site’s host name, your
site’s word count and the language codes you have enabled. Nothing is sent while no licence
key is set.
Terms: https://lingomize.com/terms — Privacy: https://lingomize.com/privacy

Groq (https://groq.com)
The proxy forwards the text to be translated to Groq’s API and returns the translation.
Only that text reaches Groq; your licence key and site details do not.
Terms: https://groq.com/terms-of-use — Privacy: https://groq.com/privacy-policy
sections.faq:
Does it duplicate my posts?

No. One post, rewritten per language at render time.

Do I need a licence key?

For AI translation, yes — the free plan is enough to try it on a real page. Everything
else (routing, hreflang, the switcher, the editor, manual translation, import and
export) works without one.

What happens if I deactivate it?

Your pages go back to their original language. Stored translations stay in the database.

I already use WPML or Polylang. Do I have to redo the work?

No. Import / Export reads what the other plugin still serves on this site and writes it
into Lingomize’s own table, page by page. Nothing is sent anywhere to do it.
sections.changelog:
0.3.4

  • AI translation of headings now reads the page title and the section under each heading,
    so a short heading such as “Ownership” is translated in the sense its section gives it.
    Run “Scan for new text” once to pick this up for existing headings, then re-translate
    them from Text: Type “Headings”, Status “AI translation”.
  • AI-translate in the editor and on the Text screen now uses each string’s real type
    (heading, SEO title, label) instead of treating everything as body text.

0.3.3

  • Language switcher flags are all the same size, and the square and circle shapes now
    render as true squares and circles.
  • A generic switcher icon (globe, translate and so on) shows once in front of the
    languages instead of before each one.

0.3.2

  • A switched-off language now leaves the language switcher for logged-in editors too, and
    the switcher preview in Settings. Editors can still open its pages to finish it.
  • In the front-end editor, accordion and tab toggles open again, so text hidden inside them
    (FAQ answers, for example) can be clicked and translated.

0.3.1

  • Switch a language off without removing it: visitors no longer see it, while its
    translations stay and can still be finished and previewed.
  • “Don’t translate these pages” takes one rule per row: is exactly, starts with, contains,
    ends with, or matches a pattern. Existing entries carry over unchanged.

0.3.0

  • AI translation now runs on a Lingomize licence key, with a free plan to start. Plans
    set how many original words the site may hold and a monthly AI-token allowance.

0.2.15

  • Find & Replace across all translations is now limited to administrators.
  • The page list no longer hands out draft-preview links for posts the user cannot edit.

0.2.14

  • Fixed inline CSS and JavaScript leaking onto translated pages as visible text.

0.2.13

  • First release on WordPress.org.

screenshots.caption: Every language you translate into, how far along each one is, and how much of your plan you have used.
The translation table: search, filter by page, status or type, edit in place, and AI-translate everything still untranslated.
Edit right on the page: click any text to translate it by hand, AI-translate it, or keep it as written.
Progress by page, per language — open any page straight into its translations.
Translation rules: words never to translate, translations to force, and pages to leave alone.
The language switcher, with a live preview while you choose names, flags or icons.
